sections.heading: 4. Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most repeated failure is the number moving between the seat map and the payment screen. thumbsuprun recalls the Rolling Stones run: the venue carried a set general admission price, then buyers reaching the payment step saw it jump $50, $70, $90, and plenty paid anyway because nobody expects a carted price to change before checkout [TpXJCfuFf4o @ 00:09:44]. Scott Cramer shows a friend's Shania Twain order listed at $227 each turning into $291 apiece on the final screen, a 30% bump on the very last step of the transaction [kFsH01UthzA @ 00:11:23]. Follow The Why documents the queue version from the Oasis reunion: fans watched a standing ticket listed around 135 pounds, queued for hours, and reached the front to find it over 350, same ticket, same day, with backlash loud enough that Britain's competition watchdog investigated [cmeE4rZAlVk @ 00:06:11]. Profit Mechanics explains why the trap lands on nearly everyone: a $60 headline becomes $90 once service, facility, order processing and email delivery fees appear, and by then the buyer has already committed, so walking away feels like losing the night. Across 20,000 seats, a $30 fee stack becomes $600,000 collected before a single note is played [p8peX6mgbrw @ 00:03:24]. Every one of these is a cost-basis error waiting to happen if the cart price gets logged as the buy price.

The second trap is assuming resale margin survives the fee cascade. Scott Cramer walks it through: a $50 listed ticket checks out at $75, so a holder who resells must ask $75 just to break even, the next buyer pays at least another $25 in fees, and the platform has now pulled an extra $50 out of one $50 seat, repeating on every transfer after that [kFsH01UthzA @ 00:07:45]. Business Made Simple puts both sides on one receipt: list an $80 ticket at $150 and the buyer sees $187.50 after a 25% buyer fee, while the site often takes a cut from the seller as well [VBp4zpS7F3o @ 00:08:42]. Why It Costs flags the floor that gets ignored: a GAO sample averaged secondary fees at 31% of listed price before fees, and CRS says weak demand can leave resellers with outright losses, so an expensive listing guarantees nothing [tH7bLaJI6ZE @ 00:08:16]. Firstpost shows the downside live on Cowboy Carter: resale collapsing to a reported $35, more than 3,200 unsold seats on the Los Angeles opening night, over 5,500 still sitting for the New Jersey date added for high demand, and nearly half the Atlanta floor open while the platform claimed 94% sold [nAgJ_xD_wuE @ 00:02:54]. A superstar name is not the same thing as superstar resale demand.

The third failure cluster is the on-sale itself. Follow The Why logs the Eras Tour collapse on November 15, 2022: 3.5 billion requests in one day, four times Ticketmaster's previous peak, 2 million tickets sold, and the Friday public sale canceled entirely because nothing was left to sell [cmeE4rZAlVk @ 00:03:59]. Inside Edition captured the street-level damage: one fan landed nosebleed seats after a five-hour wait, another was kicked out of line after queuing since 10 a.m., and a mother and daughter went from next in line to behind 2,000 others [qQIN_PDMcPA @ 00:00:39]. Prof AI Unfiltered adds that internal messages later published by Senate minority staff described several system parts failing, old legacy pages going down, rate limiting, a password server outage and older checkout technology, with no single root cause identified [enPVz7BsM7Q @ 00:02:31]. Then comes the speculative listing trap Scott Cramer describes: a third-party seller lists tickets before the show even goes on sale, at high rates, without holding them, hoping a bot can scrape seats later; if it cannot, the buyer is simply out of luck [kFsH01UthzA @ 00:21:28]. Cramer notes the Ticket Act would make speculative ticketing illegal, but doubts enforcement, since reselling bot-bought tickets is already illegal and ignored.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Capital Moves
callout.body: Clear each gate before committing money to a primary buy or posting a resale listing; every one maps to a loss or reversal practitioners hit firsthand.
items: Enter the waiting room for the very first presale: early buyers see true face value before the platform gathers data to convert seats to official platinum or raise face values [thumbsuprun — TpXJCfuFf4o @ 00:06:35].
Re-verify the price on the final payment screen: a Shania Twain order listed at $227 each turned into $291 apiece, a 30% bump on the last step [Scott Cramer — kFsH01UthzA @ 00:11:23].

Underwrite resale against the fee drag and weak demand: secondary fees averaged 31% of listed price in the GAO sample, and weak demand can leave resellers with losses [Why It Costs — tH7bLaJI6ZE @ 00:08:16].
Do not bank on click speed: queue positions are handed out essentially by lottery, so the fastest fiber in the state can still draw number 80,000 [Follow The Why — cmeE4rZAlVk @ 00:02:53].

chapters.pull_quote: "In truth, the scalper moved inside the building, put on a suit, and started calling itself the official resale partner." — Profit Mechanics (p8peX6mgbrw @ 00:05:40).
action_checklist: Get into the waiting room as early as possible to catch the first wave of true face-value tickets before platinum conversion kicks in [thumbsuprun — TpXJCfuFf4o @ 00:09:06].
Compare the all-in total across sites rather than the headline price, and divide every fee line by face value to see where the total comes from [Business Made Simple — VBp4zpS7F3o @ 00:09:01].
Map the inventory before the on-sale: on average 54% of major-event tickets never reach the public, with 16% to holds and 38% to presales [Follow The Why — cmeE4rZAlVk @ 00:00:52].
Price any resale to clear the fee cascade: a $50 listed ticket that checked out at $75 must resell at $75 just to break even [Scott Cramer — kFsH01UthzA @ 00:08:02].
Benchmark tours on Pollstar average gross and average ticket price, then verify dates and ticket details on the official artist or venue page before buying [Wise Explainer — WNNmn1bxFEU @ 00:01:24].

Flag tours where the artist caps resale at face value, as Olivia Dean's face value exchange did, since those sales are capped at the original price with no added fees [Scott Cramer — kFsH01UthzA @ 00:26:05].

chapters.question_prompt: How do resellers find, acquire and flip profitable tickets, and how do season tickets fit into the model?
chapters.title: The Reseller's Playbook: Sourcing, Selection and Flipping
chapters.subtitle: Predicting profitability before buying, venue-based and sell-through-based event selection, getting more tickets past queues, Amex/Citi presale access, scaling to five-figure months, reselling season tickets four ways, buying and cancelling season tickets, and futures odds for playoff demand
chapters.executive_summary: Ticket flippers converge on one rule: buy where demand outruns seats. Ticket Flipping and Emmanuel Ak both steer operators away from headline stadium acts toward small venues, weekend dates and hometown shows. They screen those events with Spotify listeners and live inventory counts, and both work off a 25% margin benchmark or better. The street mechanics are concrete: buy just behind Ticketmaster price breaks, set Flare drop and price alerts, divide remaining tickets by capacity, and check StubHub while seats sit in the cart. Amex and Citi card presales open early access; 850 Club Credit turned $150 floor seats into roughly $390 resales. Season-ticket holder thumbsuprun says the playoffs are where the real money is made. The split is on timing: Ticket Flipping buys late on confirmed scarcity, while Emmanuel Ak buys at release in volume across roughly 70 proxied accounts.

key_metrics.label: Per-Ticket Margin Benchmark
key_metrics.value: 25% on every ticket, aiming for 9 of 10 tickets selling well
key_metrics.context: Ticket Flipping calls 25% a conservative target and says hitting it on every buy is not rocket science.

key_metrics.label: Rush Cart-to-StubHub Spread
key_metrics.value: About $300 cost vs about $570 listed = $270 profit per ticket
key_metrics.context: Emmanuel Ak checked StubHub while the Rush seats were still sitting in his cart, before he paid.

key_metrics.label: Amex Presale Floor Flip
key_metrics.value: 4 floor seats at about $150 each; 2 resold at about $390 each
key_metrics.context: Calvin Russell bought through an Amex presale for a Drake and Migos show, kept two seats and sold two.

key_metrics.label: Playoff Upper-Bowl Resale
key_metrics.value: About $180 cost resold for over $1,500 by Game 6
key_metrics.context: thumbsuprun reported resale of Bucks Finals upper-bowl season seats.

sections.heading: 1. The Practitioner Consensus
paragraphs: The baseline model is blunt. Ticket Flipping frames it as buying hot tickets and selling them for more once the event sells out. It is a business run 100% online in a couple of hours a week, with few people doing it [Ticket Flipping — JwHo6if-9Wo @ 00:01:02]. Emmanuel Ak is UK-based and roughly six years in, having started at 16. He pitches the same picture: digital tickets, an unsaturated field, and any event type from Dave Chappelle to WWE and UFC. His standing order is not to let personal interest interfere with the business [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:03:03]. He repeats it elsewhere: most beginners lose money because they are too emotional, and numbers don't lie [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:00:38]. On the sports side, thumbsuprun treats season tickets as the base inventory because they give the lowest average cost per ticket per game. The speaker monetizes them through local sales, a client list, early listing and the playoffs, which the speaker calls where the real money is made [thumbsuprun — sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:05:41]. The economic logic is the same in both camps. Acquire inventory below the price the market will bear once supply tightens, and stay detached from the fan side of the event. The only difference is which shows and which seats get bought.

Selection is where the speakers agree most. Emmanuel Ak's jackpot combo is high-demand artists, a small venue, limited dates and weekend shows. He avoids oversaturated acts like The Weeknd, favors hometown dates such as Beyoncé in Houston, and picks Friday and Saturday over Sunday. He also notes that an 80K-capacity venue across 10 dates is 800K seats nobody needs to scramble for [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:16:00]. Ticket Flipping's live venue training defines the job as determining whether the venue is too small, so that demand will exceed ticket supply. It points out that a 500 to 1,000 capacity room in New York sells out even on a Tuesday [Ticket Flipping — ajoRfqew338 @ 00:05:12]. The same channel's scarcity funnel adds that small venues move first and that the leftovers in stadiums are platinum or VIP. Standard tickets in small or GA rooms are the target [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:08:14]. Emmanuel Ak goes underground for the same reason, pointing to a 2K-capacity venue facing 20,000 fans. He says Taylor Swift's tour made him six figures, but he warns against chasing big names [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:30:24]. The consensus filter is a ratio, not a celebrity: fans divided by seats, checked before any money moves.

The baseline toolkit is consistent too. Ticket Flipping says brokers buy and sell mainly on Ticketmaster and StubHub, which hold 26% and 22% market share, with AXS, SeatGeek and Vivid Seats also in play [Ticket Flipping — JwHo6if-9Wo @ 00:03:05]. Emmanuel Ak sells through Listed, StubHub and Vivid Seats. He recommends at least £500 to 2K of starting capital and insists on staying liquid so money keeps cycling [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:20:57]. Early access is the other prerequisite. Matthew Josiah shows Amex presale opening up to days before the public, without needing the Platinum card. In his example, The Fray's presale ran almost three days ahead of a Friday public sale, and many seats were gone about a day and a half in [Matthew Josiah — qg3wvctM0wM @ 00:05:24]. Calvin Russell of 850 Club Credit says Ticketmaster presales usually go to Amex holders and sometimes Citi holders. He says a credit score around 670 to 680 is enough for a Green or Everyday card, and that people turn this into a business [850 Club Credit — p8CMjg4a_CI @ 00:04:33]. He has helped people open multiple Amex cards in one day, and says charge or credit cards work but probably not debit. Without capital, platform accounts and a presale card, the rest of the playbook cannot run.

sections.heading: 2. Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Seat selection starts on Ticketmaster's heat map. Ticket Flipping enables it to color seats by price, dark red for expensive and green or yellow for cheaper, and says to always target price breaks [Ticket Flipping — GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:01:25]. Front-row chasers overpay at $234, while seats one row behind sit at $125. Those can be listed at $200 for a profit while still undercutting the front. In the Cole Swindle example, the front seats run 279 and 232, then 113, then green at 89. The play is to buy the $89 seats, list them at 110 to 115, and grab $89 pit seats where they exist. Brokers target the seats just behind the break, and the speaker says those price-break seats are always going to make more profit than the seats in front of them [Ticket Flipping — GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:04:44]. Emmanuel Ak prices off comparables, averaging similar sections such as 100 versus 101. He lists $50 to $100 below market to sell fast, or above market to sell later, knowing demand peaks near the show [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:23:21]. In his Rush example, the seats cost about $300 in the cart and were listed at about $570 on StubHub, a $270 profit per ticket [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:24:33].

The scarcity method replaces hype buying. Ticket Flipping calls the old way buying at presale or onsale against everyone else for the top 20 to 30 performers. Instead, it scans Flare's Latest Availability column, which tracks Ticketmaster and AXS inventory with 24-hour and 7-day change [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:00:38]. Rule one: 500 tickets tells you nothing until you divide by capacity, since that is 2.5% of a 20,000-seat venue but 83% of a 600-seat club. Rule two: direction beats the number, so a count falling from 900 to 210 beats a flat 210. Rule three: small venues move first. The filter keeps events with 30 to 500 tickets left, Spotify popularity above 49, an onsale at least a month old and a show at least a month out. The strongest signal is under 100 to 200 left and selling 20 to 50 a day; 200 tickets selling 50 a day means four days to sellout [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:10:09]. A Chrome extension tracks tickets left, so buyers can strike near 50 remaining [Ticket Flipping — JwHo6if-9Wo @ 00:08:19]. Emmanuel Ak runs the mirror check, always scanning resale before buying because people list early or hold insider tickets [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:25:17]. Ticket Flipping says niche demand can return 25%, 50% or even 100% margin.

Acquisition runs through four doors. Ticket Flipping says 99% of brokers use presales, onsales, drop alerts and price alerts. Presales give the best prices and seats but need a password and cap buyers at 4 to 8 tickets, while secondary price alerts allow an unlimited amount of seats [Ticket Flipping — NGFBVOXqxpA @ 00:03:25]. In Flare, a drop alert on nine favorite sections fires by Slack and email when seats are added. A StubHub price alert can be set at $45, under an $87 minimum. Emmanuel Ak scales the primary side with proxies: a fixed IP per account and no VPNs. He once ran about 150 accounts and now runs about 70 on two devices, noting that 20 tickets at £500 is £10,000 [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:14:48]. He then cross-lists through Listed to Vivid Seats, TickPick, TicketSwap and StubHub in about 30 minutes a day. He also uses vouched WhatsApp and Facebook groups for instant, zero-fee payouts. thumbsuprun adds a local layer: Facebook, Craigslist and street sales carry no fees. Repeat buyers become a client list, which turns into warm leads at playoff time [thumbsuprun — sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:03:17].

callout.title: Edges the working flippers actually use
callout.body: Four small habits separate a profitable buy from a stuck ticket, straight from the operators running them.
items: Buy the row where the price drops, not the front row: $89 seats behind a 113 break list at 110 to 115, and brokers are targeting just behind the break [Ticket Flipping — GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:04:15].

Watch for held inventory: releases can push a count from 500 back to 700, so look for two or three large drops relative to capacity before trusting the trend [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:11:21].

List season seats as soon as the schedule drops, since holders know their seat locations before the general sale; thumbsuprun cites $75 per ticket six months out in Calgary [thumbsuprun — sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:04:57].

Don't stop at your own card: Citi Strata adds Citi Entertainment plus Mastercard presales, and The Credit Nerd says to check every presale available for an event [The Credit Nerd — JS9sO0Fx9A0 @ 00:02:23].

sop_steps.title: Screen the event on demand versus seats
sop_steps.action: Compare city-level Spotify listeners, weekend dating and hometown status against venue capacity.
sop_steps.detail: On Dave, Emmanuel Ak counted 1M London listeners against a venue under 100K, leaving about 900,000 fans who can't get tickets [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:06:57].

sop_steps.title: Confirm scarcity with the inventory curve
sop_steps.action: Divide tickets left by capacity and confirm a daily downtrend rather than a flat count.
sop_steps.detail: A raw count of 500 tells you nothing until you divide it by capacity; buy into a falling curve, not a dud with no movement [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:02:23].

sop_steps.title: Buy at the price break with resale verified
sop_steps.action: Pick seats just behind the heat-map price break, then check StubHub while they sit in the cart.
sop_steps.detail: Target price breaks on Ticketmaster [Ticket Flipping — GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:01:25]; the Rush cart check showed $300 seats listing near $570 [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:24:19].

sop_steps.title: Cross-list, price off comps, and recycle cash
sop_steps.action: Push inventory through Listed to multiple secondaries, price against comparable sections, then reinvest.
sop_steps.detail: Listed cross-lists to Vivid Seats, TickPick, TicketSwap and StubHub, fulfills orders and delists on sale, in about 30 minutes a day [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:16:42].

sections.heading: Section 3: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The sharpest split between these operators is timing. Emmanuel Ak loads up at release and scales through account count. He runs proxies with a fixed IP per account and no VPNs, ran roughly 150 accounts at one point, and now holds about 70 across two devices. He frames the payoff as 20 tickets at £500 producing £10,000 instead of one capped login [ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:11:52]. Calvin Russell of 850 Club Credit works the same early window through card presales. He bought four floor seats at about $150 apiece roughly three months out and sold two at about $390 each a month to six weeks later, clearing the card bill in between [p8CMjg4a_CI @ 00:05:43]. Ticket Flipping calls hype-driven presale and onsale buying the old way, a brawl over the same top 20 to 30 performers. Instead, they wait until onsale is at least a month old and buy only where remaining inventory drops every day. They read the count against capacity: 500 left is 2.5% of a 20,000-seat room but 83% of a 600-cap club [hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:02:23]. The Credit Nerd sides with the skeptics, stating that a presale guarantees neither tickets, lower prices, nor better seats [JS9sO0Fx9A0 @ 00:03:51].

Selection logic splits on headliners versus rooms. Emmanuel Ak calls high-demand artists, small venues, limited dates and weekend shows the jackpot combo. He tells students that Friday and Saturday dates beat Sunday and warns off oversaturated acts like The Weeknd. He separately notes that 80,000 capacity across 10 dates puts 800,000 seats on sale [RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:16:00]. Yet the same operator says his Taylor Swift tour run made six figures in profit. He still tells students not to chase big names and to hunt underground acts, such as a 2,000-capacity venue facing 20,000 fans [ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:29:15]. Ticket Flipping works venue-first. In their view, the job is deciding whether the venue is too small for the demand, and they claim a 500 to 1,000 capacity New York room sells out even on a Tuesday [ajoRfqew338 @ 00:05:12]. Their own live research complicates that weekday call. At Bowery Ballroom, Greg Freeman, at roughly 5 million listeners, sat unsold on Tuesday and Wednesday, while the smaller Lemon Twigs sold out Friday and Saturday. On demand signals, Ticket Flipping treats Spotify as the best gauge of an artist's current popularity [JwHo6if-9Wo @ 00:06:49]. Emmanuel Ak cautions that labels buy likes and streams, so raw engagement numbers can mislead.

Exit channels and pricing posture split again. thumbsuprun argues that selling locally means no fees, a direct client connection and the best negotiated price. He rates a repeat client list as even stronger: it grows to 5, 10, 15 or 30 buyers who become warm leads in the playoffs, which he calls the stretch where season tickets pay [sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:00:42]. Emmanuel Ak also takes zero-fee instant payments through WhatsApp and Facebook groups, but only in vouched groups because of scams [ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:19:07]. His volume runs through Listed, which cross-lists to Vivid Seats, TickPick, TicketSwap and StubHub and takes him about 30 minutes a day. On price, he averages comparable sections, such as section 100 against 101. He then lists $50 to $100 under market to move fast, or above market to sell later [ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:23:21]. Ticket Flipping refuses to chase undercutters. On a live board with StubHub listings at $35, the trainer said he would hold at $94 or higher and warned that you do not really want to be pricing down at the bottom [ajoRfqew338 @ 00:23:03]. One camp races the floor for turnover; the other protects margin and waits for scarcity to arrive.

sections.heading: Section 4: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The first trap is the buyer's own head. Emmanuel Ak says most beginners lose money because they are too emotional, so he builds his selection process on numbers instead of taste [RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:00:38]. Ticket Flipping shows where that emotion costs cash on the seat map. Buyers chasing the front rows paid $234, while seats one row back cost about $125. Those seats can be listed at $200 for a profit while still undercutting the front row [GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:01:41]. The same channel says that 99% of the time you do not want platinum tickets because they are overpriced. It also flags dynamic pricing as a trap: a $50 primary ticket gets relabeled as an $80 platinum seat once resale sits at $80 [hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:12:52]. The fix Emmanuel Ak teaches is a live comparison before checkout. Keep the tickets in your cart and check the resale market first, because people list early or hold insider tickets. He did this on Rush seats that cost about $300 and were listed near $570, about $270 profit per ticket [RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:25:17]. Skip that check, and an operator ends up buying at or above what the secondary market will actually pay, with no margin left to cover fees or a slow sale.

The second trap is fake scarcity. Ticket Flipping lists four warnings from their inventory-tracking method [hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:11:21]:
- Held inventory released back into a show can push the count from 500 up to 700. They want two or three large drops relative to capacity before trusting a trend.
- Duds show few tickets left but no movement.
- Dynamic pricing hides the real get-in.
- Some shows simply lack demand, with primary at $50 while secondary sits at $45.
They add that there can always be one or two people selling for a loss. Judge the majority of listings across StubHub, Vivid Seats and TickPick, not the first few [hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:13:38]. Emmanuel Ak warns that labels buy likes and streams, so a big social following can mislead anyone who does not cross-check Spotify cities and venue size [RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:01:36]. In live venue research, Ticket Flipping watched Avery Anna, near 9 million listeners, sit unsold 23 days out. The trainer said to reconsider when get-in prices run four times face, $50 against $200, and told buyers to be careful with flips less than a week out [ajoRfqew338 @ 00:10:54]. A low count with no daily sales is not a signal; it is a stall.

The third trap is operational and capital drag. Ticket Flipping warns that secondary-market buys carry transfer delays, so an operator needs time to receive, list, sell and transfer the tickets out. Primary queues can also drop you at position 10,000 with 15 to 30 minute waits and 4 to 8 ticket caps [NGFBVOXqxpA @ 00:04:09]. Emmanuel Ak tells operators to stay liquid and says it is sometimes better to skip events than tie up money in dead stock [ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:32:36]. Season-ticket holders face a different bleed. thumbsuprun cautions that across 81 MLB home games you cannot profit on every game, and names three main pitfalls that can lose quite a bit of money [sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:05:56]. Hermanos F.C. shows the counterparty side [x2psJ5xGp18 @ 00:08:57]:
- Juan's added Inter Miami seat landed on the opposite side of the stadium.
- Reps went unresponsive for about two months.
- Friends were double-charged $280 instead of $70 on playoff tickets.
- His debit card was charged anyway as he decided to cancel.
- His group of ten is each paying $1,000, which he puts at $20,000.
Margin on paper means nothing if cash, transfers or the seller of record fail.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Any Buy Goes Through
callout.body: Each gate comes straight from a loss, stall or reversal that a named operator reported. If a buy fails any of these checks, kill it.
items: Run the cart check: compare the resale market before paying, as with Rush seats bought at about $300 and listed near $570 [Emmanuel Ak — RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:25:17].
Divide remaining tickets by capacity and require a real daily downtrend, not a 500 count that can jump back to 700 [Ticket Flipping — hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:11:21].
Confirm you have time to receive, list, sell and transfer out before committing to secondary-market buys [Ticket Flipping — NGFBVOXqxpA @ 00:04:09].
Skip any event that would tie up money in dead stock, and stay liquid for the next buy [Emmanuel Ak — ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:32:36].

chapters.pull_quote: "The price break seats are always going to make more money and let you make more profit than the seats in front of them." — Ticket Flipping (GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:04:44).
action_checklist: Turn on the seat heat map and buy just behind the price break, such as $89 seats listed at $110 to $115 (Ticket Flipping, GORTWFnPPt0 @ 00:03:18).
Filter for 30 to 500 tickets left, Spotify popularity above 49 and an onsale at least a month old before buying (Ticket Flipping, hw92haJDs9Y @ 00:04:48).
Check Spotify monthly listeners and top cities against venue capacity before committing capital (Emmanuel Ak, RsyNgibgVJY @ 00:06:57).
Set drop alerts on sold-out sections and secondary price alerts below the current market price (Ticket Flipping, NGFBVOXqxpA @ 00:04:28).
Cross-list through Listed, and sell in WhatsApp or Facebook groups only when they are vouched (Emmanuel Ak, ETQnblEeP94 @ 00:16:42).
Build a repeat client list, send it renewal pricing and games, and work those warm leads at playoff time (thumbsuprun, sQtHQZ6UoRM @ 00:02:34).
